rule_metadata.title: Allow Exceptions in Microsoft Defender Firewall via Registry

rules.rule_text:
title: Allow Exceptions in Microsoft Defender Firewall via Registry
id: c69fc6a2-607d-4530-b7d1-75823af1bde4
status: experimental
description: 'Detects the degradation of the system firewall security by the DoNotAllowExceptions
  policy value being

  set to 0 (DWORD 0x00000000), which re-enables application and port exceptions in
  the Microsoft

  Defender Firewall and can restore network paths that a hardened profile would block.

  '
references:
- https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/da209017000b9812e8bc5f4e8db6499430ee2aadc72ef896964cffdfd896f143/behavior
- https://app.any.run/tasks/8d4113a8-5403-4367-a79f-4ce4978d9bdb
- https://www.zscaler.com/fr/blogs/security-research/malvertising-targeting-european-transit-users
- https://www.trendmicro.com/vinfo/us/threat-encyclopedia/malware/trojan.win32.zbot.e
author: frack113
date: 2026-10-13
tags:
- attack.defense-impairment
- attack.t1686.003
logsource:
  category: registry_set
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains: \Services\SharedAccess\Parameters\FirewallPolicy\
    TargetObject|endswith: \DoNotAllowExceptions
    Details: DWORD (0x00000000)
  filter_main_svchost:
    Image:
    - C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe
    - C:\Windows\SysWOW64\svchost.exe
  condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
- Unknown
level: medium
regression_tests_path: regression_data/rules/windows/registry/registry_set/registry_set_allow_defender_firewall_exceptions/info.yml
